paper.title: Provable Benefits of Policy Learning from Human Preferences in Contextual Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Offline tabular contextual bandit with human rating feedback (h-model)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline policy learning from a fixed i.i.d. dataset (not an interactive bandit problem).
unmapped: offline dataset of n i.i.d. (state, action, rating) samples drawn from sampling distribution d
ratings are h(r(s,a), eps) with eps ~ N(0, sigma^2), h-bar strictly monotone (biased reward), h a degree-q polynomial in eps, symmetric noise (Conditions 1-3)
learner knows an estimate c_V V^2 of the rating variance bound
settings.definition_quote: we propose a new model under which the rating $\widetilde{r}(s,a)$ can be expressed with $\widetilde{r}(s,a) = h(r(s,a),\epsilon)$, where $h(\cdot, \cdot)$ is a general, deterministic transformation and $\epsilon$ is a random variable sampled from $\cN(0,\sigma^2)$ ... we are given an offline dataset $\cD = \{(s_i,a_i, \widetilde{r}_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Offline tabular contextual bandit with pairwise human preferences (BTL)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline policy learning from a fixed i.i.d. preference dataset (not an interactive bandit problem).
unmapped: offline dataset of n i.i.d. (state, action, action, preference) samples
learner knows the reward range R (used in the MLE constraint set)
settings.definition_quote: a human annotator gives a binary response $y = \{0,1\}$ following a Bernoulli distribution when asked to compare two state-action pairs ... $P(y|s,a,a') = \frac{\exp(r(s,a^y))}{\exp(r(s,a^0))+\exp(r(s,a^1))}$. The learner is given a dataset $\cD' = \{(s_i,a_i^0,a_i^1,y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$

settings.name_in_paper: Single-state two-action comparison: rating with sub-Gaussian noise vs biased BTL preferences
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline comparison of sample sizes for rating vs preference data (not an interactive bandit problem).
unmapped: compares the offline sample sizes needed by rating (sub-Gaussian additive noise on biased reward, uniform coverage) and biased-BTL preference data to identify the best action w.p. 1-delta
settings.definition_quote: Consider any single-state bandit instance with $\cA=\{a_1,a_2\}$ and $0 \le \bar{h}(r(a_1)) < \bar{h}(r(a_2)) \le 1$.

bound.regime: n >= c(delta, c_b, c_V, q, sigma, R)

symbols.R_max: upper bound R on the true reward range [0,R]

conditions: applies to Algorithm 1 (LCB with variance-based penalty) only
sampling distribution satisfies Assumption 1 with C* = 2
hard instance: single state, A = n^2 actions

source.label: thm:Cstar
source.quote: For any fixed constant $0 < \delta < 1$, there exists a contextual bandit instance with initial state distribution $\rho$ such that if one samples a dataset $\cD$ of size $n \ge c(\delta,c_b,c_V,q,\sigma,R)$ using a sampling distribution $d$ satisfying Assumption \ref{assumption:Cstar} with $C^\star = 2$ and runs Algorithm \ref{alg:LCB} on $\cD$, the output policy $\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB}$ must suffer constant suboptimality, i.e., $\EE_\cD[\SubOpt(\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB})] = c_0 R$

results.notes: Suboptimality of offline learned policy mapped to simple_regret. Lower bound for a specific algorithm.

bound.regime: n >= c(delta, c_b, c_V, sigma, R)

conditions: example rating model h(r,eps) = r^2 + r^2 eps|eps|, rewards in [0,1]

source.label: cor:Cstar
source.quote: the output policy $\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB}$ must suffer constant suboptimality, i.e., $\EE_\cD[\SubOpt(\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB})] = c_0$, where $c_0$ is a universal constant

results.notes: Specialisation of Theorem 1 to the quadratic example model.

symbols.hbar_inv: inverse of the expected bias function h-bar
symbols.V_Rsigma: upper bound on the standard deviation of ratings h(r,eps)

source.label: thm:uniform
source.quote: if one samples a dataset $\cD$ of size $n \ge \max\{48\sigma^4, 60\}$ using a sampling distribution $d$ satisfying Assumption \ref{assumption:uniform} with $d(s,a) = \frac{1}{SA}$ ... the output policy $\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB}$ must suffer suboptimality at least $\EE_\cD[\SubOpt(\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB})] = c_0\cdot \bar{h}^{-1}(\sqrt{V_{R,\sigma}^2/n})$

conditions: example rating model h(r,eps) = r^2 + r^2 eps|eps| with eps ~ N(0, sigma^2)

source.label: cor:uniform
source.quote: the output policy $\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB}$ must suffer suboptimality at least $\EE_\cD[\SubOpt(\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB})] = \frac{c_0\sigma}{n^{1/4}}$, where $c_0$ is a universal constant.

results.notes: sigma is the std of the Gaussian eps.

symbols.sum_sa: sum over covered state-action pairs (s,a) in X
symbols.d_bar: min over covered pairs of d(s,a)
symbols.hbar_inv: inverse of the expected bias function
symbols.V_Rsigma: upper bound on std of ratings
symbols.q: polynomial degree of the rating noise in eps

conditions: learner knows the noise distribution (q and V) to set the penalty
tuning: b_m = c_b sqrt(V^2 log^q(SA/delta)/m), c_b universal constant

source.label: thm:upper-bound
source.quote: Suppose Assumption \ref{assumption:Cstar} holds. For any fixed constant $0 < \delta < 1$, if one runs Algorithm \ref{alg:LCB} with $b_m = c_b\sqrt{\frac{V^2_{R,\sigma}\log^q\frac{SA}{\delta}}{m}}$ ... as soon as $n > 8\log\frac{2SA}{\delta}/\bar{d}$, ... with probability $1-\delta$, the suboptimality ... satisfies $\SubOpt(\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB}) \le c_0\sum_{(s,a)\in\cX}d_\rho^{\pi^\star}(s,a)\cdot \bar{h}^{-1}(\ldots)$

results.notes: K denotes the number of actions A.

conditions: example rating model h(r,eps) = r^2 + r^2 eps|eps|, rewards in [0,1]
tuning: b_m = sqrt(64 sigma^4 log(SA/delta)/m) + 8 sigma^2 log(SA/delta)/m

source.label: cor:upper-bound
source.quote: Suppose Assumption \ref{assumption:Cstar} holds. ... if one runs Algorithm \ref{alg:LCB} with $b_m = \sqrt{\frac{64\sigma^4\log\frac{SA}{\delta}}{m}} + \frac{8\sigma^2\log\frac{SA}{\delta}}{m}$, ... with probability $1-\delta$, ... $\SubOpt(\widehat{\pi}_{\rm LCB}) \le 2\sum_{(s,a)\in\cX}d_\rho^{\pi^\star}(s,a)\left(\frac{256\sigma^4\log\frac{SA}{\delta}}{n\cdot d(s,a)}\right)^{1/4} + \ldots$

results.notes: The paper's expression is ambiguous about whether the second term is inside the sum; recorded as inside.

source.label: thm:comp
source.quote: Denote $\gamma = \frac{1}{2+\exp(R\sqrt{SA})+\exp(-R\sqrt{SA})}$. Suppose Assumption \ref{assumption:Cstar-comp} holds. ... with probability $1-\delta$, the suboptimality of the output policy $\widehat{\pi}_{\rm PMLE}$ satisfies $\SubOpt(\widehat{\pi}_{\rm PMLE}) \le c_0C^\dagger R(\ldots)$

results.notes: Stated as a special case of Theorem 3.2 of Zhu et al. (2023) with modification; re-proved in the tabular setting here.

conditions: single state, two actions, 0 <= hbar(r(a1)) < hbar(r(a2)) <= 1
rating: additive sub-Gaussian noise with variance proxy sigma^2, n_{a1} = n_{a2}

source.label: thm:both-bias
source.quote: let $n_{\text{rate}}$ be the total number of samples needed to learn the optimal action with probability at least $1-\delta$ in the human rating setting ... and let $n_{\text{pref}}$ be the number of samples needed ... with observation model \eqref{eq:BTL-biased}. It always holds that $\frac{n_{\text{rate}}}{n_{\text{pref}}} < 0.25\sigma^2.$

results.notes: Ratio of sample-size thresholds derived from Chernoff/Hoeffding bounds, not a standard performance guarantee; recorded as quantity other.
